answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to multiply by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can post or claim rewards. A kernel of rules assigns weight only to activity backed by that stake, while a thread of linked accounts cannot earn more influence merely by splitting into fresh names. If an attacker spreads identities across an island of accounts, each still needs its own locked capital; coordination can expose the cluster, but the direct cost is funds immobilized and at risk of forfeiture for proven abuse.
